picks.file: Georg Braun & Frans Hogenberg - Dresden and Leipzig.jpg
picks.what: View of the walled city, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: bright colored copy; trimmed to the ‘Leipzigk’ panel (Dresden above cut); walls, Pleissenburg and church towers

picks.file: Gezicht op Leipzig Die statt Leijptzig (titel op object), RP-P-2018-979.jpg
picks.who: unknown engraver, published by Frederik de Wit
picks.why: detailed bird’s-eye view of the walled city with its churches and castle; key and margins cut

picks.what: General view across the meadows, engraving in Bechstein’s Album der Haupt- und Residenzstädte Europa’s
picks.why: whole skyline with the town hall tower and church towers; title cut

picks.file: Market place and Hotel de Ville, Leipsig (i.e., Leipzig), Saxony, Germany-LCCN2002720591.jpg
picks.what: The market square and the Old Town Hall, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: the city’s signature square in color; border and caption cut

picks.what: View over the old town, photograph
picks.why: sharp high view over the center’s roofs with St. Thomas Church

gaps: P0: no candidates; P5: nothing usable (cloud shots, wartime aerials, a Taunus postcard)
notes: #14 bears Frederik de Wit’s imprint; the Rijksmuseum dates the plate 1657, and its composition copies the 1617 Braun and Hogenberg bird’s-eye view (#1, #7), which I passed over for P1 so the two picks don’t repeat one view. Alternative for P1 if preferred: #1 (1617 colored bird’s-eye, 1683 px). P3 alternatives: #18 (1846 panorama from Niesens Haus, a very long strip) and #20 (1815 aquatint of the Grimma suburb after the battle, would need event:true).
